newsitem.title: ISRAEL: Hamas blasts Israeli-PLO peace deals.
newsitem.headline: Hamas blasts Israeli-PLO peace deals.

text.p: The Islamic militant group Hamas on Thursday launched a scathing attack on Israeli-PLO peace moves and vowed to resume armed struggle against the Jewish state.

Calling Jews "sons of monkeys and pigs," the statement underscored a rift within Hamas, the Islamic Resistance Movement, over its relations with Yasser Arafat's Palestinian Authority and his peace partner Israel.
Hamas has gradually returned to the limelight following harsh Israeli and PLO crackdowns because of four suicide bombings in Israel in February and March that killed 59 people.
The statement vowed Hamas's armed wing, the Izz el-Deen al-Qassam, would renew attacks on Israel.

In a reference to Israeli leader Benjamin Netanyahu, it said: "The armed struggle, striking the Zionist targets and escalating the intifada are the true response to the Nazi policies of the government of terrorist Netanyahu."
Hamas described the 1993 Israeli-PLO self-rule deal negotiated in the Norwegian capital as "the Oslo conspiracy" and said the fact that talks were stalled proved Israel wasn't interested in peace.
"The Oslo conspiracy continues, proving once again the correctness of our position towards this frivolous agreement that was signed by some in the name of the Palestinian people," the statement said.

"The struggle and holy war (jihad) did not end so that we should drop our weapons. Thousands are still held in the dark Zionist Nazi jails, tasting the bitterness of torture methods every day," it added.

The statement, distributed in the West Bank town of Ramallah to mark the group's ninth anniversary on December 14, contrasted sharply with conciliatory stands aired by the group's leaders in the Gaza Strip last week.
"The zero hour is approaching," it said. "We call for continuing strikes at the herds of settlers and their coward soldiers wherever they are and to respond to them with all possible means," it said.

Last Friday, Hamas leaders unveiled a new political programme during a rally in self-ruled Gaza licensed by the Palestinian Authority in which they endorsed peace negotiations with Israel to establish a Palestinian state in the West Bank and Gaza Strip, including East Jerusalem.
Hamas leaders later said the programme reflected a growing rift within Hamas leadership between those in Gaza and the West Bank and those abroad over the future of the group.
The Palestinian Authority has destroyed much of the Hamas infrastructure in crackdowns launched after the February and March suicide bombings.
